extracted.intended_audience: general readers and book buyers looking for LGBTQ+ Pride reading recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: A curated editorial list of books for LGBTQ+ Pride reading, showcasing titles by LGBTQ+ authors across genres, themes, identities, and formats with short descriptive blurbs. Intended to help readers discover celebrated, timely, and thematically relevant books for Pride and year‑round reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship: books by LGBTQ+ authors
rubrics_metrics.description: "Celebrate Pride all year long with books by LGBTQ+ authors!" — selection centers works written by LGBTQ+ authors as a primary organizing principle for the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blurb explains purpose: selections range "from inspirational memoirs to irresistible romances" that "honor the journeys of LGBTQ+ individuals and the larger movement for love, acceptance, and equality for all." Examples: memoirs (Tomorrow Will Be Different), fiction (Giovanni’s Room), biography (Marsha).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The list deliberately spans multiple genres: "from inspirational memoirs to irresistible romances" and includes novels, story collections, poetry, memoir, biography, graphic novels, essays, history, satire, thrillers, and speculative/genre fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the list: poetry (The Bronze Arms), graphic novel (Simplicity), historical/photographic history (We Are Everywhere), epic fantasy (The Spear Cuts Through Water), thrillers (The Long Con), satire (Gay Science).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic focus on queer experiences (chosen family, friendship, coming of age, desire, identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selections emphasize themes central to LGBTQ+ life such as chosen family, queer friendship, coming of age, longing/desire, identity, and the work of becoming oneself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted blurbs: Small Joys — "an ode to queer friendship and chosen family"; Open, Heaven — "a novel about desire, yearning, and the terror of first love"; A Sharp Endless Need — "coming of age, first love." Use these themes to guide inclusion and descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with gender, masculinity, and critiques of the gender binary
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes works that interrogate masculinity, patriarchy, and the harms of the gender binary and that prompt readers to rethink gender norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Before They Were Men — explores "masculinity, patriarchy, and misogyny" and concludes "men and boys may be the ones suffering the most under the gender binary right now." Such critical engagement is a selection criterion for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centered trans and nonbinary perspectives and trans writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The list highlights trans and trans-adjacent work and explicitly recognizes titles that "push the limits of trans writing" or profile trans figures and experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Stag Dance is said to "push the limits of trans writing"; Marsha is "the first definitive biography of the revolutionary activist Marsha P. Johnson"; selections include trans authors and Black transgender luminaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and political relevance to LGBTQ+ movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles that document, contextualize, or reflect on LGBTQ+ history and political milestones are included to illuminate movement history and activism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Stonewall Reader (archives for Stonewall anniversary), We Are Everywhere (photographic history of the Queer Liberation Movement), Marsha (biography of Marsha P. Johnson), and memoirs that connect personal story with rights struggles (Tomorrow Will Be Different).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional tone and voice (tender, funny, celebratory, interrogatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and blurbs emphasize distinctive tonal qualities — tenderness, humor, rage, lyricism, celebration, interrogation — as markers of a work's appeal and fit for the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blurb adjectives: "tender and generous," "acidly funny," "celebratory without apology," "hilarious and profound," "searing and crushing." These tone descriptors are used to recommend fit for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary recognition and acclaim as a signal of quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of awards, prize recognition, and prominent curatorial picks (Booker Prize, Oprah’s Book Club, Lambda Literary Award, New York Times bestseller) are used to signal literary merit and reader interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A Brief History of Seven Killings noted as "Booker Prize Winner"; The Emperor of Gladness associated with "Oprah’s Book Club"; A Sharp Endless Need linked to Lambda Literary Award. Such tags are featured in listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and boundary-pushing (formal or conceptual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that are formally inventive or conceptually daring — e.g., speculative premises, genre-mixing, or audacious narrative strategies — are emphasized as noteworthy inclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Immaculate Conception uses cutting-edge SCAFFOLD technology premise; Stag Dance praised for "inventive audacity"; The Spear Cuts Through Water described as "ambitious and profound" and unlike anything you've read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural, geographic, and identity diversity of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The list intentionally includes authors and stories from diverse cultural, racial, and national backgrounds (Nigeria, Iran, China, Korea/Asian American, Latine, Black, Muslim, Jewish) to reflect a wide spectrum of queer experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Necessary Fiction (contemporary Nigeria), Martyr! (son of Iranian immigrants), Cinema Love (gay men in rural China), I Leave It Up to You (Korean American setting), Muñeca (queer Latine witch), Last Night at the Telegraph Club (Chinese American 1950s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and availability information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry lists physical format (paperback/hardcover/graphic novel), price, and preorder/buy links, indicating consideration for reader accessibility and purchasing options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every book entry shows format (e.g., Paperback $18.00, Hardcover $30.00), and some display "Preorder" or "Buy from Other Retailers," which helps readers find and purchase recommended titles.
